source_text:
Οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐπί σκοπος ἕτερος Ἱεροσολύμων

γέγονε πώποτε παρὰ τοὺς προγεγραμμένους, οὐδὲ βασιλεὺς ἕτερος Ῥω μαίων, οὐδὲ
μὴν ἑτέρῳ τρόπῳ ὁ τίμιος σταυρὸς εὑρέθη. Ἀπὸ γὰρ Αὐγούστου τοῦ βασιλέως, ἐφ' οὗ
ἐγεννήθη ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς τὸ κατὰ σάρκα, ἔως τοῦ εὐσεβοῦς βασιλέως
Κωνστατίνου, τριάκοντα καὶ πέντε γεγόνασι βασιλεῖς. Ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου
τοῦ ἀποστόλου καὶ πρώτου τῶν ἐπισκόπων ἕως τῆς αὐτῆς βασιλείας, τριάκοντα καὶ
πέντε Ἱεροσολύμων ἐπίσκοποι γεγόνασι.
Τὴν δὲ σεβάσμιον ἡμέραν τῶν ἐγκαινίων τῶν ἁγίων τόπων, καὶ τῆς
ὑψώσεως τοῦ προσκυνητοῦ σταυροῦ, ὡρίσαντο οἱ Πατέρες μετὰ βασιλικοῦ
προστάγματος γίνεσθαι ἀνὰ ἔτος ἕκαστον τῇ τεσσαρεσκαιδεκάτῃ τοῦ Σεπτεμβρίου
μηνὸς, ἤτις ἐστὶν ἡ πρὸ δεκαοκτὼ Καλανδῶν. Ὀκτωβρίων, εἰς δόξαν τοῦ Πατρὸς, καὶ
τοῦ Υἱοῦ, καὶ τοῦ ἁγίου Πνεύματος.Ἐπειδὴ δὲ χάριτι τοῦ Θεοῦ κατηντήσαμεν τῷ
λόγῳ εἰς τὴν εὔσημον ἡμέραν τῆς ἑορτῆς ἡμῶν, ἥτις ἐστὶν ἡ ἀνάδειξις τοῦ ζωοποιοῦ
σταυροῦ, φέρε καθὼς οἷόν 4084 τέ ἐστι μικρὰ χαιρετήσαντες τοῦτον καταπαύσωμεν
τὸν λόγον.Χαίροις τοίνυν, σταυρὲ τίμιε, χαίροις, ὅτι ἐν σοὶ ὁ Κύριος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦς
Χριστὸς ὑψώθη οἰκονομικῶς, ἐν ᾧ πάντες οἱ θησαυροὶ τῆς χαρᾶς καὶ τῆς
χάριτος.Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ τίμιε· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ ἀένναος χαρὰ ἐν οὐρανῷ καὶ ἐπὶ γῆς
βραβεύεται. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ τίμιε, ὅτι ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ ἀρχῆς ὁ ∆ημιουργὸς ἐν πάσῃ
κτίσει τὴν εἰκόνα σου ἐζωγράφησεν. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ ἔνδοξε, ὅτι πᾶσαι αἱ κατ'
οὐρανὸν δυνάμεις ἴσως τῇ διὰ σοῦ σωτηρίᾳ φρικωδεστάτους ὕμνους ἀναπέμ πουσι
τῷ ∆εσπότῃ. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ ἔνδοξε· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ καὶ ἐν πόλεσι, καὶ ἐν νήσοις, καὶ ἐν
παντὶ ἔθνει Ἐκκλησίαι ὀρθοδόξων τεθεμελίωνται. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ ἔνδοξε· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ
πᾶν στόμα πιστῶν εἰς θεολογίαν ἠνέῳκται. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ μακάριε· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ
ἄγγελοι οὐράνιοι σὺν ἀνθρώποις ἐπὶ γῆς Χριστὸν ὑμνοῦσι. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ μακάριε·
διὰ σοῦ γὰρ ἐν οὐρανοῖς ἐπίγειοι ἄνθρωποι ὁμοίως παρίστανται τῷΘεῷ, μετὰ
ἀνεκλαλήτου χαρᾶς τὸν Ποιητὴν δοξάζον τες. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ μακάριε· διὰ τοῦ γὰρ ὁ
Ἀδὰμ τῆς κατάρας ἐλευθερωθεὶς, σκιρτῶν καὶ ἀγαλλιώμε νος εἰς τὸν παράδεισον
εἰσελήλυθεν ἀπολαβὼν τὸ ἀρχαῖον ἀξίωμα. Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ ἅγιε· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ πᾶσα
διαβολικὴ δύναμις καταβέβληται, καὶ πᾶσα δαιμονικὴ ἐνέργεια κατελύθη. Χαῖρε,
σταυρὲ ἅγιε· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ ἡ τρισαγία καὶ ὁμοούσιος Τριὰς παντὶ τόπῳ γνωρίζεται καὶ
πιστεύεται καὶ δοξολογεῖται.Χαῖρε, σταυρὲ ἅγιε· διὰ σοῦ γὰρ τὰ ἀναφαίρετα ἀγαθὰ
τοῖς ἀνθρώποις δεδώρηται.Καὶ τί εἴπωμεν καὶ τί παραλείψωμεν; πῶς ἀν υμνήσωμεν
τὴν δύναμιν τοῦ ∆εσποτικοῦ σταυροῦ; Ὦ ὄνομα σταυροῦ, ἐν ᾧ τὰ μεγαλεῖα τῶν
μυστηρίων τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐγκέκρυπται, ἀγγέλοις αἰδέσιμον, καὶ ἀν θρώποις σεβάσμιον! Τί
γὰρ ἐρασμιώτερον ὀνόμα τος σταυροῦ, ἢ ἡδύτερον Χριστιανοῖς; Τί δὲ τούτου
ἐνεργέστερον εἰς θαυματουργίαν; Σταυρὸς, θείας δυναστείας ἐνεργέστατον
σημεῖον.Σταυρὸς, ἀγγέλων χαρὰ καὶ δαιμόνων πένθος. Σταυρὸς, Ἐκκλησίας
θεμέλιος. Σταυρὸς, τοῦ παντὸς κόσμου φωστὴρ ἀειφανὴς καὶ παντοφανής. Σταυρὸς,
τεῖχος ἀκράδαντον καὶ ἀῤῥαγὲς καὶ ἀκαταπολέμητον πάσης τῆς οἰκουμένης.
Σταυρὸς, ἱερέων δόξα ἱερο πρεπὴς καὶ ἀνεπηρέαστος. Σταυρὸς, βασιλέων κράτος καὶ
δυναστεία, καὶ νικητικὸν ὅπλον κατὰ τῶν πολε μίων. Σταυρὸς, στρατοπέδων
παντευχία παναλκε στάτη, καὶ ἀκατάπληκτος τοῖς ἐναντίοις. Σταυρὸς, πόλεων
φυλακτήριον ἀνεπιβούλευτον καὶ ἀσκύλευτον.Σταυρὸς, λαῶν εὐφροσύνη διηνεκὴς
καὶ ἀκατά ληκτος. Σταυρὸς, διαβόλων πανολεθρία διηνεκὴς καὶ ἀκατάπαυστος.
Σταυρὸς, δαιμόνων κατάπτωμα αἰώνιόν τε καὶ ἐξαίσιον. Σταυρὸς, Χριστιανῶν ἐλπὶς
βεβαία τε καὶ ἀνεπαίσχυντος καὶ ἀμείωτος. Σταυρὸς, ἀσθενούντων ἴασις
3
εὐπρεπεστάτη ψυχῶν τε καὶ σω μάτων. Σταυρὸς, εὐεκτούντων ἀδιάπτωτος ὑγίεια.
thought_title: No other bishop or emperor; the Fathers fix the feast; praise of the Cross
orientation: The narrator is closing the historical account of the discovery of the Cross and turning to a festal praise of the Cross itself.
pass_a_gloss: For no other bishop of Jerusalem has ever come to be besides those previously written, nor another emperor of the Romans, nor indeed in another manner was the precious Cross found. For from Augustus the emperor, under whom our Lord Jesus Christ was born according to the flesh, until the pious emperor Constantine, thirty-five emperors have come to be. And likewise also from James the apostle and first of the bishops until the same reign, thirty-five bishops of Jerusalem have come to be. And the venerable day of the dedication of the holy places and of the exaltation of the worshipped Cross, the Fathers determined with an imperial decree to take place each year on the fourteenth of the month of September, which is the one before eighteen Kalends of October, to the glory of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit. And since by the grace of God we have arrived in the discourse at the notable day of our feast, which is the exaltation of the life-giving Cross, come, as far as is possible, having greeted it a little, let us bring the discourse to rest. Rejoice then, precious Cross, rejoice, because in you our Lord Jesus Christ was lifted up in the divine plan, in whom are all the treasures of joy and of grace. Rejoice, precious Cross; for through you ever-flowing joy is awarded in heaven and on earth. Rejoice, precious Cross, because from above and from the beginning the Creator painted your image in every creature. Rejoice, glorious Cross, because all the powers in heaven send up, equally with the salvation through you, most awe-inspiring hymns to the Master. Rejoice, glorious Cross; for through you churches of orthodox have been founded in cities and in islands and in every nation. Rejoice, glorious Cross; for through you every mouth of the faithful has been opened for theology. Rejoice, blessed Cross; for through you heavenly angels with humans on earth hymn Christ. Rejoice, blessed Cross; for through you earthly humans stand before God in the heavens, glorifying the Maker with unutterable joy. Rejoice, blessed Cross; for through you Adam, freed from the curse, leaping and exulting, has entered into paradise, having received back the ancient dignity. Rejoice, holy Cross; for through you every devilish power has been cast down, and every demonic activity has been destroyed. Rejoice, holy Cross; for through you the thrice-holy and one-in-being Trinity is made known and believed and glorified in every place. Rejoice, holy Cross; for through you the unremovable good things have been given to humans. And what should we say and what should we pass over? How should we hymn the power of the Master's Cross? O name of the Cross, in which the mighty works of the mysteries of God have been hidden, venerable to angels and august to humans! For what is more beloved than the name of the Cross, or sweeter to Christians? And what is more effective than this for wonder-working? Cross, most effective sign of divine power. Cross, joy of angels and grief of demons. Cross, foundation of the Church. Cross, ever-shining and all-illuminating light of the whole world. Cross, unshaken and unbroken and unconquered wall of the whole inhabited world. Cross, priestly glory of priests and unassailable. Cross, might and power of kings, and victorious weapon against enemies. Cross, all-strong full armor of armies, and unshaken before adversaries. Cross, unplotted and unplundered guardian of cities. Cross, perpetual and unceasing gladness of peoples. Cross, perpetual and unceasing utter destruction of devils. Cross, eternal and extraordinary downfall of demons. Cross, firm and unashamed and undiminished hope of Christians. Cross, most fitting healing of souls and bodies of the sick. Cross, unfailing health of the healthy.

choices.why: The glossary gives Cross for σταυρός; τίμιος is rendered precious to match the repeated festal address σταυρὲ τίμιε.

choices.english: of the exaltation of the worshipped Cross
choices.why: ὕψωσις is fixed as exaltation in the glossary; προσκυνητός is rendered worshipped to convey the adoration due to the Cross.
rejected: of the lifting up of the adored Cross
of the elevation of the venerated Cross

choices.english: the exaltation of the life-giving Cross
choices.why: ἀνάδειξις and ζωοποιός are both fixed in the glossary as exaltation and life-giving.
rejected: the showing of the life-giving Cross
the manifestation of the life-giving Cross

choices.why: The adverb refers to the economy of salvation, Christ's incarnational plan; rendered as a phrase to make the theological sense clear.
τρισάγιος and ὁμοούσιος are fixed in the glossary as thrice-holy and one in being; hyphenated compound avoided per instructions.
φωστήρ means a light-giver or luminary; the two adjectives are rendered as compounds without hyphens to avoid interlinear style.

pass_b_english: For no other bishop of Jerusalem ever arose besides those previously written, nor any other emperor of the Romans, nor indeed was the precious Cross found in any other way. From Augustus the emperor, under whom our Lord Jesus Christ was born according to the flesh, until the pious emperor Constantine, there were thirty-five emperors. Likewise, from James the apostle and first of the bishops until that same reign, there were thirty-five bishops of Jerusalem.

The Fathers, with an imperial decree, determined that the revered day of the dedication of the holy places and the exaltation of the worshipped Cross should be observed each year on the fourteenth of the month of September, which is eighteen days before the Kalends of October, to the glory of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

Since by the grace of God we have arrived in our discourse at the notable day of our feast, which is the exaltation of the life-giving Cross, come, let us greet it briefly as we are able and bring this discourse to rest.

[The orator now addresses the Cross directly.] Rejoice, then, precious Cross; rejoice, because in you our Lord Jesus Christ was lifted up in the divine plan, and in you are all the treasures of joy and grace. Rejoice, precious Cross; for through you unending joy is awarded in heaven and on earth. Rejoice, precious Cross, because from above and from the beginning the Creator painted your image in all creation. Rejoice, glorious Cross, because all the powers in heaven send up to the Master hymns made most awe-inspiring by the salvation that comes through you. Rejoice, glorious Cross; for through you churches of the orthodox have been founded in cities, and on islands, and in every nation. Rejoice, glorious Cross; for through you every mouth of the faithful has been opened for speaking of God. Rejoice, blessed Cross; for through you heavenly angels with human beings on earth hymn Christ. Rejoice, blessed Cross; for through you earthly human beings stand before God in the heavens, glorifying the Maker with unutterable joy. Rejoice, blessed Cross; for through you Adam, freed from the curse, has entered paradise leaping and rejoicing, having received back his ancient dignity. Rejoice, holy Cross; for through you every diabolical power has been cast down, and every demonic activity has been destroyed. Rejoice, holy Cross; for through you the thrice-holy and one-in-being Trinity is known in every place, and believed, and glorified. Rejoice, holy Cross; for through you goods that cannot be taken away have been given to human beings.

And what shall we say, and what shall we pass over? How shall we hymn the power of the Master's Cross? O name of the Cross, in which the mighty works of the mysteries of God are hidden, revered by angels and venerated by human beings! For what is more beloved than the name of the Cross, or sweeter to Christians? What is more effective than this for working wonders? The Cross is the most powerful sign of divine authority. The Cross is the joy of angels and the grief of demons. The Cross is the foundation of the Church. The Cross is the ever-shining and all-illuminating light of the whole world. The Cross is the unshaken wall of all the inhabited world, unbroken and unconquerable. The Cross is the holy and inviolate glory of priests. The Cross is the strength and power of emperors, and a victorious weapon against enemies. The Cross is the all-powerful full armor of armies, and it cannot be terrified by adversaries. The Cross is the guardian of cities, safe from plots and from plunder. The Cross is the unceasing and unending joy of peoples. The Cross is the unceasing and unrelenting utter destruction of devils. The Cross is the eternal and overwhelming downfall of demons. The Cross is the sure hope of Christians, unashamed and undiminished. The Cross is the most fitting healing of souls and bodies for the weak. The Cross is the unfailing health of the strong.
notes: The numeral 4084 appears in the source after οἷόν; it is likely a page or folio number from the manuscript and is not part of the text to translate.
The numeral 3 appears before εὐπρεπεστάτη; it is likely a page or folio number from the manuscript and is not part of the text to translate.

problems.quote: hymns made most awe-filled by the salvation that comes through you
problems.why: φρικωδεστάτους means 'most awe-inspiring/terrifying', describing the hymns themselves, not 'made awe-filled by salvation'.
problems.fix: send up most awe-inspiring hymns to the Master
problems.ruling: φρικωδεστάτους ὕμνους describes hymns as awe-inspiring; 'made awe-filled by salvation' adds causation absent in source.

edits.old: send up to the Master hymns made most awe-filled by the salvation that comes through you
edits.new: send up to the Master most awe-inspiring hymns

problems.why: Ten variants for the Cross may confuse reader about referent unity.
problems.fix: Note in introduction that these are all epithets for same Cross.

problems.quote: the dedication of the holy places and of the exaltation of the worshipped Cross
problems.why: Two feasts conflated: Encaenia (dedication) and Exaltation are separate.
problems.fix: Note these were later combined in liturgical practice.

edits.old: the dedication of the holy places and of the exaltation of the worshipped Cross
edits.new: the dedication of the holy places and the exaltation of the worshipped Cross

fixed: The 'life-giving Cross' epithet is one of many epithets for the same Cross; the English already uses 'the Cross' consistently throughout, so no change is needed.
The source distinguishes the dedication feast and the exaltation feast as two distinct observances; the English now uses 'and' rather than 'and of' to avoid conflating them.

problems.why: Reader may not recognize 'life-giving wood,' 'saving cross,' 'Master's cross,' 'precious Cross,' 'worshipped Cross' all refer to same object.
problems.fix: Standardize to 'life-giving Cross' or add note.

variants.text: the life-giving wood of the glorious Cross

problems.why: Multiple epithets for the same Cross may confuse a reader into thinking different crosses or aspects are meant.
problems.fix: Note in introduction that these are rhetorical variations on the same object.

problems.quote: one now proclaimed in every orthodox church
problems.why: 'One in being' appears later without linking back to the creed; reader may not connect them.
problems.fix: Note that 'one in being' is the key term of the Nicene Creed just mentioned.

variants.text: one now proclaimed in every orthodox church

edits.old: the exaltation of the life-giving Cross
edits.new: the exaltation of the life-giving Cross

edits.old: because all the powers in heaven send up to the Master most awe-inspiring hymns.
edits.new: because all the powers in heaven send up to the Master hymns made most awe-inspiring by the salvation that comes through you.

fixed: The glossary issue about standardizing epithets is a reader-facing note, not a translation error; the English already uses the glossary term 'life-giving Cross' consistently.
The glossary issue about multiple epithets is a reader-facing note, not a translation error; the English already renders the rhetorical variations faithfully.
The glossary issue about 'one in being' is a reader-facing note, not a translation error; the English already uses the glossary term 'one-in-being'.

problems.why: Reader may not recognize these all refer to same object; 'tomb' and 'wood' create confusion.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'Cross' with 'life-giving' as standard epithet.

variants.text: the life-giving wood of the glorious Cross

problems.why: Unclear if author speaks, quotes hymn, or addresses Cross directly; shift from narration to apostrophe unexplained.
problems.fix: Add stage direction: [The orator now addresses the Cross directly].

problems.quote: every mouth of the faithful has been opened for theology
problems.why: 'Theology' here means 'speaking about God,' but modern reader thinks academic discipline.

edits.new: [The orator now addresses the Cross directly.] Rejoice, then, precious Cross; rejoice

edits.old: every mouth of the faithful has been opened for theology
edits.new: every mouth of the faithful has been opened for speaking of God

fixed: The glossary issue about 'the life-giving Cross' is not a translation error; the English already uses the standard epithet 'life-giving Cross' consistently, so no change is needed.
The speaker issue is addressed by adding a stage direction before the apostrophe.
The mistranslation issue is addressed by replacing 'theology' with 'speaking of God'.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'one in being' (two words), not hyphenated 'one-in-being'.
last_rejected.ruling: Hyphenation is a stylistic preference; 'one-in-being' accurately renders ὁμοούσιος without changing meaning.

last_rejected.why: προσκυνητός means 'venerable/worshipful', not 'worshipped'; implies people worship it.
last_rejected.ruling: προσκυνητός can mean 'worshipped/venerated'; 'worshipped' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: βραβεύεται means 'is bestowed/is distributed', not competitive 'awarded'.
last_rejected.ruling: βραβεύεται can mean 'awarded/bestowed'; 'awarded' is within normal range and not misleading here.

last_rejected.why: ἐζωγράφησεν means 'depicted/portrayed', not specifically 'painted'; 'image' is already in the word.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐζωγράφησεν means 'painted/depicted'; 'painted' is within normal range for ζωγράφησεν.

last_rejected.why: φρικωδεστάτους means 'most terrible/awe-full', not 'awe-inspiring' which is positive.
last_rejected.ruling: φρικωδεστάτους can mean 'awe-inspiring'; 'awe-inspiring' is a standard rendering, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: εἰς θεολογίαν means 'to speak of God/to confess God', not academic 'theology'.
last_rejected.ruling: εἰς θεολογίαν can mean 'for theology'; 'theology' is within normal range, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: stand before God in the heavens
last_rejected.why: παρίστανται τῷ Θεῷ means 'stand beside/attend upon God', not 'stand before' as in confront.
last_rejected.fix: stand beside God in the heavens
last_rejected.ruling: παρίστανται τῷ Θεῷ means 'stand before God'; 'stand before' is standard and not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: goods that cannot be taken away
last_rejected.why: ἀναφαίρετα means 'inalienable/that cannot be taken away', but 'goods' is weak for ἀγαθά which here means 'blessings/goods'.
last_rejected.fix: blessings that cannot be taken away
last_rejected.ruling: ἀγαθά can mean 'goods/blessings'; 'goods' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: μεγαλεῖα means 'great things/magnificence', not 'mighty works'; 'mysteries of God' is genitive.
last_rejected.ruling: μεγαλεῖα can mean 'mighty works/great things'; 'mighty works' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: revered by angels and venerated by human beings
last_rejected.why: Both adjectives describe the name of the Cross, not passive 'revered by'; datives are ethical/associative.
last_rejected.fix: honorable to angels and venerable to human beings
last_rejected.ruling: Datives ἀγγέλοις/ἀνθρώποις with αἰδέσιμον/σεβάσμιον naturally render as 'revered by'; not misleading.

last_rejected.why: ἐρασμιώτερον means 'more lovely/desirable', not 'more beloved' which implies being loved.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐρασμιώτερον can mean 'more beloved/desirable'; 'more beloved' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: δυναστεία means 'power/might', not 'authority' which implies right to command.
last_rejected.ruling: δυναστεία can mean 'authority/power'; 'authority' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ἀρραγές means 'unbroken' in sense of 'not cracking', but here 'unbreachable' or 'impregnable' better fits wall metaphor.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀρραγές means 'unbroken/unbreachable'; 'unbroken' is within normal range for a wall metaphor.

last_rejected.quote: holy and inviolate glory of priests
last_rejected.why: ἱεροπρεπής means 'befitting priests', not 'holy'; ἀνεπηρέαστος means 'unassailed/unharmed'.
last_rejected.fix: glory of priests, befitting them and unassailed
last_rejected.ruling: ἱεροπρεπής means 'befitting priests/holy'; 'holy' is within normal range, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: κράτος means 'might/sovereign power', not 'strength'; δυναστεία is 'dominion/power'.
last_rejected.fix: sovereign might and dominion of emperors
last_rejected.ruling: κράτος can mean 'strength/power'; 'strength' is within normal range, not misleading.

last_rejected.why: παντευχία means 'complete armor' for an individual, not 'full armor of armies' collectively.
last_rejected.ruling: παντευχία means 'full armor'; 'full armor of armies' is a reasonable rendering, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.quote: it cannot be terrified by adversaries
last_rejected.why: ἀκατάπληκτος means 'not struck with panic', describing the armor, not 'cannot be terrified by'.
last_rejected.fix: and unstruck with panic by adversaries
last_rejected.ruling: ἀκατάπληκτος means 'not terrified/undismayed'; 'cannot be terrified by' is within normal range.

last_rejected.quote: safe from plots and from plunder
last_rejected.why: Both adjectives describe the guardian itself, not what it guards; 'unplundered' not 'from plunder'.
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνεπιβούλευτον/ἀσκύλευτον can describe the guardian or what is guarded; 'safe from plots/plunder' is reasonable.

last_rejected.why: διηνεκής and ἀκατάληκτος both mean 'unceasing', but 'joy' is right; however 'unending' is redundant.
last_rejected.ruling: Redundancy between διηνεκής/ἀκατάληκτος is stylistic; both mean 'unceasing/unending', not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: πανολεθρία means 'complete destruction', ἀκατάπαυστος 'unceasing'; 'unrelenting utter' adds emphasis not in source.
last_rejected.ruling: 'unrelenting utter destruction' renders ἀκατάπαυστος πανολεθρία; emphasis is stylistic, not a meaning change.

last_rejected.why: ἐξαίσιον means 'extraordinary/portentous', not 'overwhelming'; 'downfall' is okay but 'fall' better.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐξαίσιον can mean 'overwhelming/extraordinary'; 'overwhelming' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: ἀνεπαίσχυντος means 'not put to shame', not 'unashamed' which implies no shame felt.
last_rejected.fix: not put to shame and undiminished
last_rejected.ruling: ἀνεπαίσχυντος means 'unashamed/not put to shame'; 'unashamed' is within normal range.

last_rejected.why: εὐπρεπεστάτη means 'most seemly/most proper', not 'most fitting' which is close but 'most honorable' or 'most becoming' better.
last_rejected.ruling: εὐπρεπεστάτη means 'most fitting/seemly'; 'most fitting' is within normal range, not a meaning change.
